sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *sin embargo* from A2 Unit 28 and *no obstante* from B1 Unit 1: both introduce a fact that goes against what you have just said. *No obstante* is a little more formal. The recognition of indigenous rights is full of such contrasts: a law is passed, "however" its application is hard.

items.spanish: El Convenio 169 es de 1989; no obstante, muchos conflictos por la consulta siguen abiertos.
items.english: Convention 169 dates from 1989; nevertheless, many conflicts over consultation remain open.

items.spanish: La Declaración de 2007 no es un tratado; sin embargo, se cita con frecuencia.
items.english: The 2007 Declaration is not a treaty; however, it is often cited.

items.spanish: Ecuador aprobó su Constitución en 2008; sin embargo, algunas comunidades piden más participación.
items.english: Ecuador approved its Constitution in 2008; however, some communities ask for more participation.

items.spanish: Colombia reconoció la diversidad en 1991; no obstante, la aplicación sigue siendo discutida.
items.english: Colombia recognised diversity in 1991; nevertheless, its application is still debated.

sections.content: *Sin embargo* and *no obstante* usually start the second clause and take a comma after them: *…; sin embargo, …*. Do not use *por eso* or *además* in their place: they do not contrast.
